item.title: Nonlocal approximation of stable minimal surfaces with prescribed number of connected components
item.description: arXiv:2611.33476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that every strictly stable classical minimal hypersurface in a Euclidean ball can be approximated, for $s$ sufficiently close to $1$, by a stable $s$-minimal surface in a smaller ball. We also give an explicit lower bound on the size of the interval of admissible values of $s$. As a consequence, we construct stable nonlocal minimal surfaces with an arbitrarily large number $k$ of connected components in a bounded region, under the quantitative condition $k \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{1-s}}$, attaining an optimal result (at least in dimensions $2$ and $3$). As part of the proof of our main result, we obtain an auxiliary result of independent interest, providing quantitative estimates for foliations of constant mean curvature embedded hypersurfaces near a stable minimal surface. The resulting foliation supplies nonlocal barriers thanks to known results of uniform convergence of the nonlocal mean curvature to the classical one when $s \to 1$.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo De Gaspari, Serena Dipierro, Ovidiu Savin, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: The Whitney sphere and tori as self-shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2611.33504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the Whitney sphere in $\C^n$ is a self-shrinker for the Hamiltonian gradient flow of volume. We construct an explicit family of Lagrangian self-shrinking tori in $\C^2$ containing infinitely many pairwise noncongruent examples. We also characterize closed connected Lagrangian immersions whose Legendrian lifts lie in a Kor\'anyi sphere by showing that, up to scaling and a unitary transformation, they factor through the Whitney immersion via a diffeomorphism for $n\geq2$ and a finite covering for $n=1$.
item.dc:creator: Jingyi Chen, Micah Warren

item.title: Geometry and Analysis of Spinor Valued Forms
item.description: arXiv:2611.33551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study spinor valued differential forms, that is, sections of the bundles $\mathcal{S}_p=\mathcal{S}\otimes\Lambda_p\otimes L$ of spinor valued $p$-forms twisted by a $U(1)$ line bundle $L$, on compact even-dimensional Riemannian spin (or $\mathrm{Spin}^\mathbb{C}$) manifolds. We develop the algebra of spinor valued forms: the chirality, grading and duality involutions, the bilinear tensors built from spinor valued forms and the Fierz-type identities they satisfy, and the action of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R})$ generated by Clifford multiplication and contraction, which we use to decompose the space of spinor valued forms into irreducible components and to construct an adapted orthonormal basis. We introduce the twisted exterior derivative and coderivative, the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators and, more generally, the natural first-order operators on spinor valued forms, as well as the twisted Hodge and signature operators, and derive their conformal transformation laws. We obtain the Weitzenb\"ock formulas for the twisted de Rham and Dirac Laplacians, express the curvature terms through the Weyl tensor, the Ricci tensor, the curvature of $L$ and the bilinear tensors of the spinor valued forms, and derive vanishing theorems, heat trace invariants and index formulas. Finally, in four dimensions we use these Weitzenb\"ock formulas to construct non-negative functionals whose absolute minima define two generalizations of the Seiberg--Witten monopole equations to right spinor valued $p$-forms, one based on the Dirac operator and one on the twisted de Rham Laplacian, and discuss the resulting integrability conditions.
item.dc:creator: Ivan G. Avramidi, Forest Good

item.title: Equivariant cohomology of stacky Lie group actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33604v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work we introduce equivariant cohomology for Lie groupoids and differentiable stacks. For Lie groupoids equipped with a strict action of a Lie 2-group, we define the corresponding equivariant cohomology via the Borel model and establish its Morita invariance. We also construct a simplicial Cartan model and prove that, under standard compactness assumptions, it recovers the equivariant cohomology defined via the Borel model. In the framework of stacky Lie group actions, we show that if a connected and \'etale stacky Lie group acts on a differentiable stack admitting an equivariant atlas, then the stacky action admits a strict presentation by a Lie 2-group action. Furthermore, we prove that different choices of equivariant atlases yield equivariantly Morita equivalent presenting actions, giving rise to a well-defined notion of equivariant cohomology for differentiable stacks. As an application, we compute the equivariant cohomology of toric symplectic stacks.
item.dc:creator: Daniel L\'opez Garcia, Cristian Ortiz, Roberto Villaflor

item.title: Reeb stability for singular Riemannian foliations
item.description: arXiv:2611.33609v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a global Reeb stability theorem for singular Riemannian foliations on compact connected manifolds using the semi-local model developed by Alexandrino et al. We show that all leaves are compact if and only if the foliation is infinitesimally closed, and there exists a compact leaf with a linear holonomy groupoid which is proper at that leaf. These conditions are also equivalent to the existence of a smooth map to a Euclidean space whose fibers are exactly the leaves. The proof combines a local criterion for strong stability with compact transverse leaves, Molino's structural theory, and polynomial descriptions of local leaf spaces. Around a closed leaf, we show that the linear holonomy groupoid realizes the original foliation precisely when the infinitesimal foliation is homogeneous. When the infinitesimal foliation is closed, properness of this groupoid yields an associated-bundle model whose compact structure group is its isotropy group. We also characterize the existence, near a compact leaf, of a Hausdorff model Lie groupoid which is proper at that leaf. As an application, we obtain stability results for maps whose connected fiber components form singular Riemannian foliations. We compare linear holonomy with Fernandes's reduced Lie algebroid holonomy and with formal outer holonomy. Finally, we prove that, for every infinitesimally closed singular Riemannian foliation, the compactly supported tangent vector fields form a locally finitely generated involutive module inducing the original leaf partition.
item.dc:creator: Mateus de Melo, Laura Ribeiro dos Santos, Ivan Struchiner

item.title: On the rigidity of generalized cylinders
item.description: arXiv:2611.33641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove pointed Gromov--Hausdorff rigidity of cylinders $N\times\mathbb R^d$ whenever $N$ is a compact Einstein manifold rigid as a Ricci shrinker.
item.dc:creator: Hanbing Fang, Yu Li

item.title: Examples of Ricci limit spaces with infinite bubbles
item.description: arXiv:2611.33884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k\geq 6$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R} $, and $(X,h)$ be an $k$-dimensional smooth complete Riemannian manifold with $\mathrm{Ric}_h > \lambda $. In this paper, we construct, for each given $\epsilon >0$, a sequence of $(k+2)$-dimensional manifolds $(X\times\mathbb{S}^2 ,g_i ) \stackrel{GH}{\longrightarrow} (X_\epsilon ,d_\epsilon ) $ with $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_i} > \lambda $, such that $d_{GH} (X,X_\epsilon ) \leq \epsilon $, and $X_\epsilon $ has no open subset which is topologically a manifold. In particular, the sequence of Riemannian manifolds we construct have uniformly bounded topology, which improves the earlier examples of Hupp-Naber-Wang and Zhou.
item.dc:creator: Shengxuan Zhou

item.title: Total Curvature and Topology of Complete Euclidean Immersions: Heat Kernel and Boundary Morse Approaches
item.description: arXiv:2611.33992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two mechanisms relate the scale-invariant integral of the second fundamental form to topology at infinity of a complete Euclidean immersion. The first retains the mean-curvature potential in the Michael--Simon Sobolev inequality, establishes an ultracontractive estimate for the semigroup generated by $\Delta+|H|^2$, and uses a vector-bundle Cwikel--Lieb--Rozenblum bound to estimate spaces of $L^2$-harmonic forms. Together with the theory of nonparabolic ends, this yields $e(M)\le 1+C_n\int_M|A|^n$ for arbitrary complete immersed $n$-manifolds, $n\ge3$. The second method, under the additional assumption of finitely many single-sheeted $C^2$-asymptotically planar graphical ends, uses a boundary Morse complex and the normal Gauss-map area formula to prove $\sum_j b_j(M;\F)+e(M)-2\le\TA(F)$. It supplies an explicit end coefficient and bounds ordinary Betti numbers. We provide proofs of both mechanisms, identify the exact role of their respective hypotheses, and discuss minimal and Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian specializations.
item.dc:creator: Lei Zhang

item.title: Three-dimensional harmonic critical metrics for the Einstein-Hilbert functional and self-similar Ricci flows
item.description: arXiv:2611.34037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We address the three-dimensional harmonic analogue of Hilbert's variational problem: does criticality of the Einstein-Hilbert functional under volume-preserving Chen-Nagano variations force constant sectional curvature, and how is this rigidity related to Ricci flow and topology? Starting from the known characterization of compact harmonic critical metrics as gradient Ricci solitons, we use Ivey's classification to show that such metrics on closed three manifolds are precisely the space-form metrics, equivalently the stationary metrics of the volume-normalized Ricci flow. We also describe residual gauge one-forms, establish transversality of the Chen-Nagano gauge to infinitesimal diffeomorphism directions, and give explicit self-similar flows. The normalized Ricci-flow velocity is an admissible Chen-Nagano variation for n > = 3, and the smooth Poincar'e theorem admits an equivalent formulation in terms of the existence of harmonic critical metrics
item.dc:creator: Sergey E. Stepanov, Irina I. Tsyganok

item.title: Smooth approximation of one-sided minimizing CMC hypersurfaces with isolated singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.34080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a CMC hypersurface with an isolated singularity, given by the boundary of a set of finite perimeter, that minimizes the prescribed mean curvature functional on one side. If a varifold tangent at the singularity is a non--flat regular cone of multiplicity--1 that minimizes perimeter on the side occupied by the blow--up, then we show that, in a small neighborhood of the singular point, there exists a sequence of smooth CMC hypersurfaces, with the same prescribed mean curvature, that converges to the initial hypersurface. We also establish the full CMC variational equation and regularity for minimizers of a class of singular obstacle problems.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Leskas

item.title: Sharp Barycentric Costs in Teichmuller Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.32448v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The affine Beltrami fiber over a closed hyperbolic surface has a quadratic normal response whose least vertical $L^2$ energy equals the tangent norm dual to the hyperbolic cotangent supremum norm. We prove this calibration using a curvature identity and exact localized responses. Its strictness determines the energy measures of near-minimizers and, under an amplitude constraint, gives a positive excess with an explicit quadratic lower coefficient when the supporting differential has nondegenerate maxima. Pointwise Poincar'e barycenters of representatives in one fiber give a nonlinear realization: equal-weight pairs attain prescribed small outputs exactly, and their creation energy approaches the calibrated norm if and only if the output scale is negligible relative to the squared amplitude bound. Restoring the full local fiber graph has leading cost four times the squared Weil--Petersson norm. For degenerating surfaces, we identify the additive limit of the calibrated norm across persistent components and collar directions. The induced length metric completes to marked augmented Teichm"uller space and has distance $\frac{\pi}{2}\sum_i \ell_i + O((\sum_i \ell_i)^2)$ to a fixed pinching stratum. Systole-dependent estimates also yield exact nonlinear realizations along degenerating families.
item.dc:creator: Hangyu Li

item.title: A singular Lawson cone minimizing the fractional perimeter in dimension seven
item.description: arXiv:2611.33496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the nonlocal Lawson cone constructed by Davila, del Pino, and Wei (J. Differential Geom. 2018) in $N=7$ minimizes the fractional perimeter for all sufficiently small orders $s$. Thus nonlocal minimal surfaces can have singularities already in dimension $7$. This contrasts both with the classical theory, where the first singular example occurs in dimension $8$ (Bombieri-De Giorgi-Giusti, Invent. Math. 1969), and with the fractional theory for orders $s$ close to $1$ (Caffarelli-Valdinoci, Adv. Math. 2013).
item.dc:creator: Giampiero Palatucci

item.title: Tori without contractible closed geodesics
item.description: arXiv:2611.33500v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that a Riemannian 2-dimensional torus has no contractible closed geodesics if and only if it admits a geodesic foliation.
item.dc:creator: Anton Petrunin

item.title: On the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point for the Yamabe equation in all dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.33646v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point of solutions to the Yamabe equation in every dimension $n\ge 25$. On every closed, connected, smooth $n$-dimensional manifold $M$ of positive Yamabe type and at any prescribed point $p\in M$, we construct a smooth metric $ \widehat g$ and a sequence of smooth positive solutions to the Yamabe equation blowing up at $p$, such that the first nonzero covariant derivative of the Weyl tensor at $p$ has any prescribed order $l$ satisfying $l\ge 6$ when $25\le n\le 29$, $l \ge 4$ when $30\le n\le 51$, and $l\ge 2$ when $n\ge 52$. Moreover, $|\nabla_{ \widehat g}^{l}W_{ \widehat g}|>0$ everywhere on $M$. Earlier constructions realize every strictly higher order as the first nonzero order, while the known Weyl vanishing results exclude every lower first nonzero order. Thus the endpoint cases $l=6,4,2$ were the only ones left open, and are settled here. In particular, the order-two examples show that the compactness criterion $|W|+|\nabla W|>0$ is sharp. At the endpoints, the construction arranges global and localized metric perturbations to interact at leading order in a limiting functional. For $l=2,4$, anisotropic polynomial ansatzes involving two orthogonal algebraic Weyl tensors remove a distinguished translation degeneracy and produce $C^1$-stable saddle points. For $l=6$, a different polynomial ansatz produces a nondegenerate local minimum. Higher prescribed orders are obtained by separating the perturbation that determines the limiting functional from the one that prescribes the Weyl derivative.
item.dc:creator: Liuwei Gong, YanYan Li, Anthony Matos

item.title: Singularities in global pluripotential theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.33697v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This book is an expanded version of the author's lecture notes at the Institute for Advanced Study in Mathematics (IASM) at Zhejiang University. We systematically develop the theory of plurisubharmonic singularities on compact K\"ahler manifolds and relate it to the non-Archimedean pluripotential theory and toric pluripotential theory.
item.dc:creator: Mingchen Xia

item.title: Conjugate points on Lie groups with left-invariant metrics
item.description: arXiv:2408.03854v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove sufficient conditions for the existence of conjugate points along geodesics of a left-invariant metric on a Lie group, using a reformulation of the index form in terms of the adjoint action. In the compact semisimple case, with an arbitrary left-invariant metric, we show that all geodesics must have a conjugate point, and we give upper and lower bounds on conjugate times. In particular this applies to the left-invariant metrics on $SU(n)$ and $SO(n)$ which are of importance in fluid dynamics and rigid body motion, and yields estimates for the diameter and injectivity radius. We also establish criteria in the noncompact case: we show that every closed nonhomogeneous geodesic has a conjugate point, and determine explicit conditions for them in the three-dimensional unimodular case. For homogeneous geodesics, we relate conjugate points to Lagrangian stability, and Eulerian stability of the corresponding steady velocity. Finally, we obtain as by-products criteria for conjugate points in general homogeneous spaces, by lifting the problem to the total Lie group of the quotient and using a result of O'Neill. Through several examples, we show that our theorems apply when well-known criteria relying on positive Ricci curvature or other curvature bounds fail, and in some cases even when Ricci curvature is negative along a certain geodesic.
item.dc:creator: Alice Le Brigant, Leandro Lichtenfelz, Stephen C. Preston

item.title: A Riemannian viewpoint on the Amari-Cencov $\alpha$-connections and Proudman-Johnson equations
item.description:
arXiv:2508.00371v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a new geometric interpretation of the Amari-Cencov $\alpha$-connections $
abla^{(\alpha)}$ from information geometry: On the space of densities $\operatorname{Dens}_+(M)$, we show that there exist Riemannian metrics $G^\alpha$, which we call $\alpha$-Fisher-Rao metrics, whose Levi-Civita connections are $
abla^{(\alpha)}$. With the exception of $\alpha=0$ (the Fisher-Rao metric), these metrics are non-invariant to the action of the diffeomorphism group $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$, even though the connections are invariant. This gives a new way of interpreting the geodesics of the $
abla^{(\alpha)}$ as energy-minimizing curves. On the space of probability densities $\operatorname{Prob}(M)$, we show that the same phenomenon holds for $\alpha\in \{-1,0,1\}$ and that the $\alpha$-connections are not metric otherwise. We show that $
abla^{(\alpha)}$-geodesics on this space can be interpreted as radial projections of straight lines on appropriate hyper-surfaces, and use this geometric picture to obtain geodesic convexity for any $\alpha\in \mathbb{R}$. In addition, we prove analogous results for appropriate metrics and connections on $\operatorname{Diff}(M)$, which, for the case $M=\mathbb{R}$, imply that the generalized Proudman-Johnson equations on the real line are the Euler-Arnold equations of non-right invariant metrics. Finally, in the finite-dimensional case, we show that $
abla^{(\alpha)}$ can be metric or non-metric depending on the considered statistical model.
item.dc:creator: Martin Bauer, Alice Le Brigant, Cy Maor

item.title: Deformations of Locally Conformal Parallel Spin(7) Instantons
item.description: arXiv:2511.09161v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the infinitesimal deformation theory of $Spin(7)$-instantons on compact locally conformal parallel (LCP) $Spin(7)$ manifolds, that is, $Spin(7)$ manifolds whose fundamental 4-form satisfies $d\Phi=\theta\wedge\Phi$ with a closed, non-exact Lee form $\theta$. We show that the gauge-fixed linearized instanton equations are equivalent to a kernel problem for a twisted Levi-Civita Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}^-_A-\mathcal{A}_\theta\colon\Gamma(\mathcal{S}^-\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)\to\Gamma(\mathcal{S}^+\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)$, compute the zeroth-order term $\mathcal{A}_\theta$ explicitly, and show that its pointwise squared operator norm equals $\frac{49}{64}|\theta|^2$. Combined with the Lichnerowicz--Weitzenb\"ock formula and Ivanov's scalar curvature identity, this yields a sufficient condition for rigidity, which we show can never be satisfied by flat connections. Indeed, the trivial connection is never rigid: its deformation space contains $H^1(M;\mathbb{R})\otimes\mathfrak{g}$. Our main result concerns the product LCP manifolds $N\times S^1$, where $N$ is a compact nearly parallel $G_2$ manifold: for the pull-back of a $G_2$-instanton $B$ on $N$ we prove $\mathcal{H}^1_{Spin(7)}(\mathrm{pr}^*B)\cong\mathcal{H}^0_{G_2}(B)\oplus\mathcal{H}^1_{G_2}(B)$. This reduces the deformation theory of such instantons to the nearly parallel $G_2$ case, shows that this containment is an equality for the trivial connection, and produces non-flat examples on the Hopf manifold $S^7\times S^1$ and on other products with homogeneous nearly parallel $G_2$ manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Ey\"up Yal\c{c}{\i}nkaya

item.title: Nice bases for Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2603.16540v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The concept of a nice basis for a Lie algebra was introduced to study the Ricci curvature on nilpotent Lie groups equipped with a left-invariant metric. Despite the many applications in differential geometry, for example in the construction of Einstein manifolds, very little is known about the existence and number of nice bases on a given Lie algebra. This paper studies this question for three classes of Lie algebras, namely direct sums, almost abelian ones and nilpotent Lie algebras associated to a graph. As an application we compute the number of nice bases for Lie algebras up to dimension $3$, and show that for a general Lie algebra the existence depends on the field over which it is defined. Moreover, for every natural number $n$ we give an indecomposable Lie algebra such that there exists exactly $n$ nice bases up to equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Der\'e, Jeroen Gantois

item.title: Curvature inequalities and rigidity for constant mean curvature and spacetime constant mean curvature surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.16707v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish curvature inequalities and rigidity results for constant mean curvature (CMC) surfaces in Riemannian manifolds and spacetime constant mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces in Lorentzian manifolds. In three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we show that the Christodoulou-Yau inequality $H^2\leq 16\pi/|\Sigma|$ ($H$ denoting mean curvature and $|\Sigma|$ area) for stable CMC spheres also holds for CMC surfaces of arbitrary topology under a new stability condition controlling only the constant mode of the second variation of area. Under an extrinsic curvature sign condition, equality forces the enclosed region to be Euclidean without additional intrinsic assumptions. We extend these results to higher dimensions and to the hyperbolic and spherical settings. In the Lorentzian setting, we develop a variational stability theory for STCMC surfaces based on the second variation of area in the mean curvature vector direction. We introduce two independent stability notions: variational stability, which recovers classical volume-preserving CMC stability for surfaces in totally geodesic spacelike hypersurfaces, and constant-mode stability. Under the dominant energy condition, either yields the sharp inequality $|\vec H|^2\leq 16\pi/|\Sigma|$. In the equality case, under suitable geometric assumptions, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the enclosed spacelike region is a Minkowski causal diamond. These results imply nonnegativity and rigidity of the Hawking quasi-local energy for stable STCMC surfaces. Finally, we analyze known spacelike and null STCMC foliations, showing that asymptotic leaves are stable under positive mass conditions, whereas the local matter density and trace-free extrinsic curvature govern the instability of local foliations.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Pe\~nuela Diaz

item.title: Einstein manifolds and extended Poincar\'{e} algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.40042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For any pseudo-Euclidean space $V \simeq \mathbb{R}^{p, q}, p \geq 3$, module $W$ over the even Clifford algebra $\text{Cl}^{0}(V)$ and $V$-valued skew-symmetric bilinear $\mathfrak{so}(V)$-equivariant form $\Pi$ on $W$, V. C\'{o}rtes constructed noncompact quaternion-pseudo-K\"{a}hler homogeneous space. In particular, such homogeneous space is always Einstein and for $p=3$ it is Riemannian. The current paper is devoted to the generalization of this construction for $p = 3$ to the case $p \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$ and an irreducible $\text{Cl}^{0}(V)$-module. As a result we construct the new series of Riemannian Einstein homogoneous spaces $M_{p, q}$ with negative scalar curvature.
item.dc:creator: D. V. Alekseevsky, A. N. Lavrov

item.title: Hessian manifolds of positive constant Hessian sectional curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.01737v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hessian structure on a manifold is a geometric structure consisting of a pair $(\nabla,g)$ of an affine connection $\nabla$ and a Riemannian metric $g$ satisfying certain compatibility conditions. It is also known as a dually flat structure in information geometry. Hessian geometry is considered to be a real analogue of K\"ahler geometry; in particular, Hessian sectional curvature corresponds to holomorphic sectional curvature in K\"ahler geometry. The standard models of Hessian manifolds with constant Hessian sectional curvature were classified by Furuhata and Kurose (2013) in the nonpositive curvature case, whereas the positive curvature case is open. In this paper, we classify the standard models in the positive curvature case. For this end, we introduce Hessian structure on quotient manifolds of K\"ahler manifolds equipped with suitable Hamiltonian actions of abelian Lie groups and realizing the standard models as such quotient manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Hakobi Sakamoto

item.title: A simple construction of smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carath\'eodory conjectures
item.description: arXiv:2610.34036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a recent announcement, Alp\"oge presented smooth counterexamples to the Loewner and Carath\'eodory conjectures and credited John-Paul Smith. We present a simpler construction of a seed by using trigonometric functions. Using this, for every positive integer $k$, we construct a smooth real-valued function on the plane, flat at the origin, whose Hessian eigenline fields share the origin as an isolated singularity of index $1+k/2$. A support-function parametrization realizes this index as an umbilic index of a non-real-analytic $C^\infty$-regular surface germ in Euclidean $3$-space. The same framework, applied to a rapidly decreasing function on the whole plane, gives a strictly convex closed regular surface with exactly one umbilic, of index $2$. This paper is self-contained with regard to the existence of an isolated umbilic of index $2$ and the construction of a counterexample to the Carath\'eodory conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Naoya Ando, Masaaki Umehara

item.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
item.description: arXiv:2611.10598v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long

item.title: Controlled Riemannian rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2611.10854v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a compact Lie group acting smoothly and freely on a compact connected manifold, we prove that the space of invariant Riemannian metrics whose symmetry group is precisely the group in question is open dense in that of all invariant metrics provided the orbit space is at least 2-dimensional. This strengthens the author's prior results to their optimal dimension bound and recovers Ebin's non-equivariant analogue to the effect that trivial-symmetry Riemannian metrics constitute an open dense set. In the process, the discussion also addresses a number of apparent gaps in said sources, pertaining to the rigidity results in question.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Chirvasitu

item.title: $G_2'$-Slodowy Slices II: Anosov Representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14503v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We find many exotic connected components of Anosov representations of surface groups in the split real group $G_2'$ that are neither $\iota$-Fuchsian deformations nor higher rank Teichm\"uller spaces. These representations are found through the non-abelian Hodge correspondence via $G_2'$-Higgs bundles that we call $\alpha$-bundles and $\beta$-bundles, which are particular cyclic Higgs bundles in the Slodowy slices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-triples associated to the simple roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$ of $\mathfrak{g}_2^{\mathbb{C}}$. We first prove that (most) $\beta$-bundles that are also Hodge bundles are $P_{\beta}$-Anosov and $\alpha$-bundles are $P_{\alpha}$-Anosov. The strategy employed is new, geometric, and general. For $\sigma \in \{\alpha, \beta\}$, we then show the locally homogeneous $(G_2', G_2'/P_{\sigma})$-manifold $\mathscr{M}_{\sigma}(\rho)$ recently described in arXiv:2510.12757, for the representation $\rho:\pi_1S\rightarrow \mathsf{G}_2'$ associated to a $\sigma$-bundle, coincides up to finite cover with the corresponding geometric structure for $\rho$ defined via domains of discontinuity by Guichard-Wienhard and Kapovich-Leeb-Porti. Consequently, we find that $\pi_1({\mathscr{M}}_{\sigma}(\rho))$ is an invariant for the connected component of $\rho$ in the space of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations. After verifying the folklore result that the $G_2'$-character variety has exactly three connected components, we conclude lower bounds for the number of connected components of $P_{\sigma}$-Anosov representations in the two non-Hitchin components, most of which are exotic. These are the first higher rank examples of connected components of a character variety containing multiple (in fact, arbitrarily many) exotic components of Anosov representations.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, Parker Evans

item.title: Superintegrable Systems and the Tractor Connection
item.description: arXiv:2611.28568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quadratic constants of motion for natural pseudo-Riemannian Hamiltonians with potential correspond to conformal Killing tensors admitting multiple Killing scales. Taking this correspondence further, we develop a dimension-independent ($n\ge 3$) framework for studying second-order superintegrable systems using conformal tractor calculus, and invariant BGG prolongation of the rank two conformal Killing equation. We apply this framework to classify second-order maximally superintegrable systems within certain natural families of Hamiltonians generated by pairs of conformally related Einstein metrics in arbitrary dimensions. We recover the second-order analogue of Bertrand's theorem as a special case.
item.dc:creator: Simon C. W. Goodwin, A. Rod Gover, Jonathan M. Kress

item.title: Killing Scales for Conformal Killing Tensors of Rank Two and Higher
item.description: arXiv:2611.29124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study which metrics in a conformal class admit a Killing tensor with prescribed conformal Killing trace-free part. We call such metrics Killing scales. We also consider whether a given conformal Killing tensor is itself a Killing tensor for some metric in the conformal class, as well as the analogous problem for conformal Killing-Yano forms. Our approach to this problem uses conformal and projective tractors, and the prolongations provided by the BGG splitting operators of the projective and conformal Killing operators. For rank two conformal Killing tensors, we characterise local Killing scales for arbitrary scales on arbitrary conformal manifolds, extending recent results that were restricted to Einstein scales on conformally flat manifolds. The criterion is expressed in terms of the scale tractor and the BGG prolongation of the conformal Killing tensor. We also obtain Killing scale criteria for higher-rank conformal Killing tensors and conformal Killing-Yano forms, under additional hypotheses involving Einstein scales and normal solutions. We describe the tractor geometry of special Einstein products, including Ricci-flat products, and use these constructions to give examples beyond the conformally flat setting.
item.dc:creator: Simon C. W. Goodwin, A. Rod Gover, Thomas Leistner

item.title: The Kao-Lai-Osting Conjecture for the Second Laplace Eigenvalue on Riemannian Two-Tori
item.description: arXiv:2611.31024v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the $k=2$ case of the Kao-Lai-Osting conjecture for the area-normalized Laplace spectrum of Riemannian two-tori: $\sup_g \lambda_2(T^2,g)\,\mathrm{Area}(T^2,g) = 8\pi^2/\sqrt{3} + 8\pi$, where the supremum is taken over smooth Riemannian metrics. No smooth metric attains this value. It is approached by a sequence in the equilateral conformal class developing a round spherical bubble, and the equilateral class is the only conformal class whose conformal supremum equals the global one. The upper bound follows from spherical folding and a sharp truncated conformal-area inequality for fundamental embeddings into $S^5$. Normal-curvature and normal-chord estimates yield high-cap area control, with exact elementary estimates on nested high-centre strips. The proof is partly computer-assisted. Rational polynomial inequalities handle the low-weight cap range and the entire residual high-cap region, the latter through exact Bernstein certificates on rational boxes, which are also checked independently in ball arithmetic. The residual product inequality is established by rigorous upper quadratures, with two independent reproducible certificates, in ball and in interval arithmetic, and exact domain-coverage checks.

item.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
item.description: arXiv:2607.13871v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Felix Finster, Christoph Krpoun

item.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
item.description: arXiv:2611.03221v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
